spans.content: Pfizer Inc.
Anticipating Upside to Guidance As We Move Through the Year Although Pipeline Remains the Focus

Heading into PFE’s 2Q earnings (8/4), we are roughly in-line with the Street for the quarter and continue to see potential upside to guidance as we move through the year. On the quarter, we forecast sales of $14.6bn (+$130mm vs cons) and EPS of $0.69 (+$0.01). And for the year overall, we estimate sales of $62.7bn (+$860mm vs cons) and EPS of $3.05 (+$0.09) which leaves us modestly above PFE’s guidance ($59.5-$62.5bn, $2.80 - $3.00).

More broadly on the story, we continue to view PFE shares as inexpensive (~9x 2027e EPS) with several assets in the company's pipeline that could make the story more interesting over time. However, we believe further derisking/data from these programs will be needed to shift investor sentiment. And here, most major data updates will come in 2027 and beyond. As a result, we remain on the sidelines with a Neutral rating and are decreasing our Dec-26 PT to $28 (from $30) following the recent Ph3 failure for Sigvotatug Vedotin in the 2L+ NSCLC setting.

- On the quarter, we are roughly in-line with the Street. Overall, we forecast sales of $14.6bn (+$130mm vs cons) and EPS of $0.69 (+$0.01 vs cons). On the topline, this includes Padcev sales of $700mm (+$70mm vs cons), Ibrance at $1.1bn (+$90mm), Eliquis sales of $2.1bn (+3% YoY, in-line), and Vyndaqel at $1.7bn (in-line).

We are also modestly ahead of PFE's guidance for the year with Eliquis upside more than offsetting COVID weakness. On the COVID business, we are roughly in-line with the Street on the quarter, although we are below PFE's COVID guidance for the year (~$4.2bn JPMe vs ~$5bn in combined sales) given ongoing TRx trends (Comirnaty -27% YoY, Paxlovid -77%). Offsetting our COVID forecasts, we see upside to Eliquis (+$270mm vs cons for the year). And with neither COVID or Eliquis core to the story at this point, we see more limited value being attributed by the market to any beat / miss on these products. Overall, this leaves us modestly above PFE's guidance with sales of $62.7bn (vs $59.5-62.5bn guide) and EPS of $3.05 (vs $2.80 - $3.00).

- Sentiment remains low on PFE but we believe it will take pipeline progression to shift views on the stock. Investor sentiment remains depressed on the story with investors broadly seeing 1) limited downside in shares given the current valuation but 2) believing pipeline progression will be necessary for shares to re-rate. And with updates primarily centered in 2027/28+, we expect shares to be range bound from here. In the near-term, catalysts include 1) Ph1/2 data on the combination of berobenatide / GLP-1 + amylin (late-2026), 2) full Ph2 atopic dermatitis data for the company's Trispecific antibody, and 3) Ph3 Mevrometostat data post-abiraterone (July '26 PCD).
Neutral
